analysis.investment_thesis: Bandhan Bank is a financial institution — explicitly excluded from the Magic Formula because deposits are raw material (not debt), EV calculations are meaningless, and ROIC comparisons are distorted. Evaluated on bank-specific metrics, ROE of 11.2% is mediocre and finance costs (CAGR 26.6%) are growing 3.4× faster than revenues (CAGR 7.8%), signalling structural NIM compression.
key_strengths: P/B of 1.14× is near book — optically cheap relative to private-sector banking peers
Forward P/E of 10.92× prices in earnings recovery; total assets grew from INR 139K Cr to INR 191K Cr in 3 years
Improving deposit diversification reduces reliance on high-cost wholesale funding
key_risks: Core microfinance franchise under structural stress — NPAs in MFI segment remain elevated post-COVID
Finance costs compounding at 26.6% CAGR vs revenue CAGR of 7.8% — margin compression is systemic, not transient
Geographic and segment concentration in Bengal/Assam microfinance makes earnings highly vulnerable to regional credit events
red_flags: Excluded from Magic Formula: financial institution — EBIT/EV and ROIC metrics are inapplicable
Finance cost CAGR of 26.6% vs revenue CAGR of 7.8% — the spread between cost of funds and asset yields is compressing dangerously
Operating CF swung from −INR 4,245 Cr (FY23) to +INR 14,808 Cr (FY24) — extreme volatility indicates poor earnings quality visibility
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula explicitly excludes banks because their balance sheets use leverage as a production input rather than a financing choice — applying EBIT/EV to a bank is mathematically nonsensical. Evaluated on its own terms, Bandhan's ROE of 11.2% is below the 15% threshold I'd want for a bank franchise, and the FY22 base profit of INR 126 Cr that drives the impressive '179% CAGR' story was COVID-distressed, making the trajectory misleading.

The more troubling signal is the cost structure: finance costs grew from INR 5,157 Cr (FY22) to INR 10,458 Cr (FY25), nearly doubling, while net revenues rose only from INR 11,536 Cr to INR 14,457 Cr. The microfinance NPA cycle has not fully played out, and the bank is transitioning its business mix under duress. Without a clearer path to 15%+ ROE and NIM stabilisation, the cheap P/B is a trap.
